name: Herby Lamb Meatballs

ingredients.name: white bread, crust removed and cut into small pieces
loosely packed fresh mint leaves, finely chopped, divided
feta cheese in brine, drained and crumbled

instructions.primary_message: Adjust oven rack to middle position and preheat oven to 400°F. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper and set aside. In a large bowl, combine bread with milk and toss to coat. Let stand, stirring occasionally, until bread is completely moist, about 5 minutes. Squeeze bread between your fingers or mash with a spoon to make sure there are no dry spots.

Add onion, egg, coriander, cumin, red pepper, garlic, 1/4 cup mint, 2 tablespoons yogurt, 1 tablespoon dill, and 2 teaspoons salt to bread mixture. Using a clean hand or spoon, stir until very well combined. Add ground lamb and, using your hand, continue mixing vigorously, squishing meat and seasonings between your fingers, until just combined and meat has taken on a slightly sticky texture; be careful not to overwork meat.

Using wet hands, roll lamb mixture into 2-ounce meatballs (about 16 total). Place on prepared baking sheet, evenly spaced apart, and cover lightly with plastic wrap. Refrigerate meatballs until firm and cold, at least 30 minutes or up to 4 hours.

In a 12-inch cast iron, carbon-steel, or stainless-steel skillet, heat oil over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add half of meatballs in an single layer and cook, undisturbed, until browned on 1 side, 1 to 2 minutes. Using tongs, carefully turn meatballs and continue to cook, turning as needed, until browned on all sides, 3 to 4 minutes. Transfer meatballs to a large plate. Repeat with remaining meatballs. Once all meatballs are browned, transfer meatballs back to skillet, and bake until an instant-read thermometer inserted into center of meatballs registers 145°F, 5 to 7 minutes (see notes).

Meanwhile, in a food processor, process feta cheese, lemon zest and juice, remaining 3/4 cup of yogurt, remaining 1/4 cup mint, remaining 1 tablespoon dill, and remaining 1/4 teaspoon salt until mostly smooth, about 2 minutes.
Spoon sauce onto a large serving plate or individual plates. Gently set meatballs on top of sauce. Garnish with dill fronds, and serve with lemon wedges.

schema_metadata.keywords: Springy Lamb Meatballs recipe, lamb meatballs, ground lamb recipe

description: These tender, juicy lamb meatballs are packed with garlic, spices, and bright fresh herbs.
notes:
Total time, including resting: 1 hr 13 min.

Optional or for serving: 2 tablespoons chopped fresh dill, divided, plus fronds for garnish; 1 tablespoon fresh juice (from 1 medium lemon), plus lemon wedges to serve

Notes: The ideal Greek-style yogurt for this recipe is one that is completely strained; many Greek yogurts in the US market are only partially strained. One good option here is Fage, which comes thoroughly strained from the start. If you have another brand that seems slightly thinner, you can place yogurt in a fine-mesh sieve set over a bowl and let stand for about 2 hours. Once the extra water has drained away, you will have a much thicker yogurt to work with.
We think 145°F is an ideal internal temperature for lamb meatballs, but if you have any health concerns such as a compromised immune system among your diners, you can cook them further to 160°F.

Make-ahead and storage: The yogurt and feta sauce can be made ahead and refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
author: Leah Colins
